newsitem.title: USA: FBI chief orders inquiry into internal memorandum.
newsitem.headline: FBI chief orders inquiry into internal memorandum.

text.p: FBI Director Louis Freeh Tuesday ordered an inquiry into whether an internal FBI memorandum alleging the agency falsified evidence in proceedings against a former federal judge was given to all parties in the case.

Alcee Hastings, Florida's first black federal judge, was acquitted in 1983 of soliciting a bribe, but later was impeached by the House of Representatives and removed from office by the Senate on the same basic evidence.
Hastings, a Florida Democrat, ran an unsuccessful campaign for governor in 1990 but was elected to the House in 1992.

Freeh said in a written statement he learned only Teusday that "an important internal FBI memorandum" written in the 1980s may not have been given to the Senate or the House, the Appeals Court or to Hastings.

"After learning of this matter, I have directed that the Senate, the House, the 11th Circuit, and Congressman Hastings be informed of the memorandum's existence, and I have further directed that copies of the memorandum be supplied to them promptly," he said.
Freeh said an FBI laboratory examiner wrote a memorandum alleging that another FBI laboratory examiner had given "innaccurate testimony ... relating to an evidence matter."
"We do not yet know if the parties were told of that memorandum or given copies of it at the time, but I have ordered a prompt inquiry to determine the facts," Freeh said.

Freeh gave no details of the contents of the memorandum, but ABC News reported that it was written by FBI agent William Tobin in 1989 and detailed 27 specific instances in which another FBI agent, Michael Malone, gave "scientifically unfounded, unqualified and biased testimony."
Hastings, who learned of the FBI document from ABC, told the network he was outraged.
"Had any of my lawyers had this information, it would have made a world of difference," he said.
"If they fabricated testimony in my cases as a U.S. District Court judge, where else did they fabricate testimony?" Hastings asked.
An internal Justice Department investigation already has turned up serious problems at the FBI's crime laboratory which could compromise a number of criminal cases in progress.

FBI and Justice Department officials said a report by the inspector general, not yet publicly released, sharply criticised the laboratory for poor management practices and sloppy handling of evidence. It raised questions about FBI procedures and contaminated evidence, they said.

The laboratory controversy erupted late last month after the FBI announced it had removed four officials from the unit in response to the investigation, including a whistleblower whose initial complaints triggered the inquiry.
Freeh said in his statement it would be up the Senate, the House and the Appeals Court to determine what relevance, if any, the newly discovered memorandum might have on the Hastings case.
"It must be clear to all that the FBI has one sole interest in this matter -- to make certain that all of the facts and all of the truth are provided to the parties and are made public," he said.
